extracted.intended_audience: central government regulatory officials, policymakers, and regulatory reform practitioners (Korea)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for Regulatory Impact Analysis (RIA), related regulatory management tools (CICO, sunset clauses, petition systems) and institutional responsibilities within the Republic of Korea. Focused on how to prepare, review, publish and use RIA statements and related processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit of regulatory registration
rubrics_metrics.description: A single regulatory provision, which is the smallest statutory unit, is now defined as a unit of regulation for registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures the objectivity and consistency of regulatory registration; the registry system is linked to the National Law Information Centre so legislative changes are reflected promptly and the general public gains easier access to regulatory information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of RIA (Article 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: RIA aims to predict and analyse the economic, social and administrative impact of a regulation through the use of objective and scientific means, and thus establish a standard which serves as the basis for determining the appropriateness of the regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RIA's purpose is to promote evidence-based rule-making and to establish an objective standard for regulatory appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to conduct RIA and prepare RIA statement (Article 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the head of a central administrative agency intends to establish a new regulation or reinforce existing regulations, he/she shall conduct a regulatory impact analysis (RIA) and prepare a RIA statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The head must also publish the RIA statement to the general public during the advance notice period; the Regulatory Reform Committee (RRC) issues guidelines on preparation and publication of RIA statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matters to be comprehensively taken into account in RIA
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing a RIA statement, the head shall conduct RIA taking account of: (1) necessity of establishing/reinforcing regulation; (2) feasibility of the objectives of regulations; (3) existence of alternative means or overlaps with existing regulations; (4) comparative analysis on costs and benefits for regulated and the public; (5) effects on small and medium enterprises; (6) whether competition-restricting factors are included; (7) objectivity and clarity of regulations; (8) administrative organisation, human resources, and required budget after establishment/reinforcement; (9) whether documents/procedures for relevant civil service are appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These nine specified matters must be considered comprehensively as stipulated in Chapter 2, Article 7 of the Framework Act on Administrative Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirement and advance notice period
rubrics_metrics.description: The head of a central administrative agency shall publish a RIA statement to the general public during the advance notice period of the proposed legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance notice is made for approximately 40 days, during which RIAS are published to the public; this supports transparency and public input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to consider multiple alternatives (at least three)
rubrics_metrics.description: All central administrative agencies are required to consider at least three alternatives when performing RIA: an existing regulation, a regulatory alternative, and a non- or less-regulatory alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All alternatives must be substantiated by cost-benefit analysis; when selecting an alternative the decision must be made rationally and objectively through comparison of analysis results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative cost-benefit analysis requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: RIA requires a quantitative cost-benefit analysis which measures various administrative costs, generally using a quantitative methodology based on the Standard Cost Model (SCM) but adjusted to Korean characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory research centres (e.g., KDI and KIPA) support and review CBA; accurate quantification of costs/benefits is foundational (and e-RIA helps automate and ensure completeness).

rubrics_metrics.name: e-RIA system obligations and features
rubrics_metrics.description: The e-RIA system obligates users to fill out all required fields in the electronic RIA form, links to the national statistical database to obtain necessary data, provides descriptions and examples for all fields, and automatically produces the RIA statement once fields are complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: e-RIA prevents omission of important data, strengthens capacity to develop better regulation, and enables quantitative comparison among alternatives (foundation for CICO).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-in, Cost-out (CICO) principle
rubrics_metrics.description: CICO is a mechanism to restrict the increase of the costs of newly introduced or reinforced regulations by abolishing or relaxing regulations that carry an equal or more amount of costs; it also aims to continuously improve existing regulations that generate unnecessary burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CICO is implemented based on net direct cost of regulation calculated through RIA; applied to 27 central administrative agencies and formally in force from July 2016 (Prime Minister's ordinance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Reform Sinmungo – petition system and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sinmungo is a platform allowing the public and businesses to file regulatory reform petitions; when a petition is filed the public official must respond within 14 days whether to accept it. If rejected petitions are deemed reasonable by the RRO, the responsible agency must justify refusal within 3 months. Urgent petitions require feedback within one week; if an urgent petition is rejected but deemed reasonable by the RRO, justification must be provided within one month. If rationale for refusal is insufficient, the RRC can issue recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sinmungo integrates all existing petition channels into a one-stop shop; as of Nov 2016 around 40% of petitions had been accepted, resulting in improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sunset clause and periodic review
rubrics_metrics.description: Sunset clause mechanisms include 'outright sunset' (automatic expiry on a specified date) and 'review and sunset' (duty to carry out review on a specified schedule) to ensure even rational regulations are periodically examined to determine grounds for remaining in force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sunset clause is considered a critical component of regulatory quality improvement because circumstances and characteristics can change, undermining validity of regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional RIA for SMEs, competition, and technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional RIAs were introduced to analyse and compare impacts concerning competition (market efficiency, competition restriction), SMEs (excessive burdens, equity among economic players), and technology (whether regulation matches pace of technological development and global standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific task forces and agencies are assigned: Fair Trade Commission for competition, Small and Medium Business Administration for SMEs (with Korea Small Business Institute support), and Korea Agency for Technology and Standards for technology; separate Regulatory Reform Task Forces conduct in-depth analysis in these fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailored Regulatory Approach for SMEs
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce differentiation of regulations based on business size to balance burdens that fall disproportionately on SMEs; when introducing/reinforcing regulations, agencies shall consider a plan to exempt micro enterprises from application of regulations for three years if necessary, or to relax burdens on small enterprises by exempting them from application of all or some regulations or by setting a temporary relief period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tailored approach has legal basis in the July 2016 Ordinance of the Prime Minister and is intended to mitigate disproportionate impacts on smaller businesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria qualifying for Simplified RIA
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain regulations may use a Simplified RIA: administrative actions that impose penalties/fines, regulations that hold legal authority delegated by higher legislation yet contain insignificant regulatory elements, procedural regulation imposed by beneficial administrative actions, regulations introduced for administrative inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simplified RIA requires a simplified cost-benefit analysis or qualitative analysis and only a single alternative to the proposed regulation; it reduces unnecessary burdens on central agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference between Standard and Simplified RIA requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard RIA: all requirements stipulated in Chapter 2, Article 7 apply and cost-benefit analysis must be reviewed by regulatory research centres. Simplified RIA: simplified/qualitative cost-benefit analysis is required instead and only a single alternative is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most regulations default to Standard RIA; simplified form is permitted for those meeting the simplified criteria to reduce preparatory burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: RIA process, review and decision responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The RIA process: central administrative agencies draft RIA statements with experts and support (SMBA, FTC, KATS) and review via internal regulatory reform committees; RIAS for significant regulations are referred to regulatory research centres (KDI, KIPA) for CBA review; the RRC classifies proposals into significant and less significant based on assessed impacts; in-person reviews are held for significant proposals; decisions by the RRC are final and must be adhered to by central agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process is multi-layered (initial drafting, internal review, technical CBA review, RRC classification/review), focusing in-depth on SMEs, competition, technology and stakeholder opinions for significant regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology for calculating direct costs (Box 3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard calculation model for direct costs includes formulae for: Administrative burdens (personnel expenses = number personnel * time per year * wage per hour * number regulated; other expenses = price * frequency per year * number regulated); Direct labour costs (same personnel formula, with time estimated via direct attainment or standard estimates and wages estimated via industry averages); Education/training costs (trainer wage, tuition fees, opportunity costs formulas); Costs of external service (consultation fees = expert fee * number experts * frequency * number regulated; installation and operating fees likewise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer direct attainment of information from regulated entities for precision; wage and time estimates may use direct data or average/standard estimates; e-RIA implements a standard calculation model for eight types of direct costs to automate totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from RIA (Article 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Framework Act does not apply to matters falling under: (1) affairs governed by the National Assembly, the Courts, Constitutional Court, Election Commission, Board of Audit and Inspection; (2) affairs relevant to criminal matters, criminal administration, and security actions; (3) intelligence and security duties under the National Intelligence Service Act; (4) matters relevant to enrolment, drafting, mobilisation and training under military service and related Acts; (5) matters relevant to military facilities, military confidentiality, and defence industries; (6) items, rates, imposition and collection of taxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These exemptions are grounded in the principle of separation of powers and national security/taxation considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance and quality assurance for RIAS (RRC role)
rubrics_metrics.description: The RRC regularly issues a guideline on the preparation of RIA statements; central administrative agencies must draft RIAS in accordance with the guideline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines aim to enhance RIA quality; RRC also conducts online and in-person reviews to classify and scrutinize regulatory proposals.
